title: Reasons for Not Disclosing Racial Composition of Prison Inmate Population and Criminal Offender Figures
what_it_is: Reasons for Not Disclosing Racial Composition of Prison Inmate Population and Criminal Offender Figures

sections.label: Minority prison representation data
sections.summary: Minorities are disproportionately represented in prison and crime statistics, and the Government is careful about releasing racial breakdown data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The fact is minorities are disproportionately represented in the prison inmate population and in crime statistics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Government has been careful about publicly releasing such data with the racial breakdown, because it might deepen racial stereotypes.

sections.label: No race-based prison statistics
sections.summary: The Government has taken the approach not to release race-based statistics for prison inmate population and criminal offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Government has on these considerations taken the approach not to release race-based statistics for prison inmate population and criminal offenders.

sections.label: Unanimous view on releasing data
sections.summary: The unanimous view was that releasing such data would not benefit the community and Singapore's society.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The unanimous view – and I underline "unanimous view" – was that it would not benefit our community and Singapore’s society.

sections.label: Prison rehabilitation and reintegration programmes
sections.summary: Prisons and MHA mobilise volunteers and use risk assessment, stage-based programmes, job placement and post-release interventions to help inmates reintegrate.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Prisons, and MHA as a whole, mobilises large number of volunteers to work with our prison inmates.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We want to make a distinct difference to their lives such that when they come out, they can actually reintegrate back into society.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That involves a number of different approaches: one, assess them when they come in into different risk categories, decide what kind of rehabilitative approach would be best suited for them and, of course, all of this applies only if they stay for some time in prisons; those in there for a few months may not benefit from these approaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Then, there are different programmes depending on whether they are in an early stage of incarceration, middle stage or late stage.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We got to try and handhold them after they leave prison: we find them jobs, try and encourage them to keep their jobs and give other kinds of interventions.

sections.label: Cross-religion prison volunteer caution
sections.summary: MHA is careful about people of one religion talking to persons of another in Prisons without clear consent, and a Malay community initiative has increased volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We are generally quite careful about having people of one religion going into the Prisons and talk to persons of another religion, unless there is clear consent, because MHA needs to be careful about these issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And Members would have heard of the very substantial initiative in the Malay community where the mosques, MUIS, community organisations, Pergas, various organisations have come together, together with the Malay Members of Parliament and office holders to increase the number of volunteers.
